sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a house in Miami Beach?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade County tax collector sends the bill, even though the city of Miami Beach sets part of the rate. The property appraiser values the parcel, and its own homepage says it does not send bills or collect tax.

Miami Beach is a barrier island city with 7.69 square miles of land, according to the Census Bureau, and an estimated 81,594 residents in July 2025. That is a small footprint for a city that size, which is why a single parcel can carry several taxing lines on one bill.

sections.h2: What is the Miami Beach millage rate for 2026?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 adopted millage chart lists Miami Beach at 5.8060 mills for city operations plus 0.2693 for city debt service. One mill is one dollar of tax for every thousand dollars of taxable value.

The chart prints two Miami Beach lines. The first totals 18.6681 mills across every taxing authority. The second adds 0.7364 and totals 19.4045. Your tax bill or the appraiser's parcel search shows which line your folio falls under.

  • The city line is only part of the bill. County, school, regional, fire and rescue, library and Children's Trust amounts sit on top of it.
  • The chart is titled as adopted rates, so these figures are final for the 2026 roll.
  • The county roll was certified on October 16, 2026, before any Value Adjustment Board changes.

sections.h2: How does the Miami Beach city rate compare with nearby cities?
sections.html:
Miami Beach sits in the middle of the pack on the county chart. Its 5.8060 city mills compare with 5.5590 for Coral Gables, 7.1080 for Miami and 3.7743 for Surfside. Bal Harbour lists 2.5132 and Key Biscayne 2.8708.

Totals tell a slightly different story because some rows carry extra lines. Surfside totals 18.4824 mills, Bal Harbour 17.2213 and Key Biscayne 15.4636, against 18.6681 on the first Miami Beach line. A seller comparing the island with a neighboring town should compare totals, not just the city line.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Miami Beach residents?
sections.html:
The 2020 count was 82,890 people, down from 87,779 in 2010, and the July 2025 estimate of 81,594 is 1.6 percent below the 2020 base. Density works out to 10,774.7 people per square mile.

Foreign-born residents make up 52.9 percent of the population, and 64.5 percent of residents age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home. About 81.4 percent lived in the same house a year earlier, so most households stay put.

  • Mean travel time to work is 26.7 minutes.
  • Per capita income is $75,054, well above the household median of $72,856 because households are small.
  • Total accommodation and food services sales were about $3.78 billion in 2022, a sign of how much the local economy leans on visitors.

sections.h2: How many people own versus rent in Miami Beach?
sections.html:
About 40.9 percent of housing units are owner occupied, per Census figures for 2020 to 2024. The median value of those owner-occupied units is $556,700, and median gross rent is $1,826.

The same Census page counts 41,600 households with 1.95 people each. Only 18.8 percent of residents are 65 or older, so many sellers here are not retirees using age-based relief. Median household income is $72,856 in 2024 dollars.

For a seller, a low owner-occupancy rate means the buyer pool often includes investors and second-home buyers. Whether you hold a homestead exemption on January 1 changes your tax picture more than anything else on the bill.

sections.h2: What are the key tax dates for Miami Beach owners?
sections.html:
Florida runs one tax cycle per calendar year, and the same dates apply in Miami Beach as everywhere else in the state.

Florida property tax calendar as printed by the Department of Revenue
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Exemption and classification filing deadline
AugustTRIM notice mailed
25 days after the noticeValue petition due with the clerk
NovemberTax bills go out
November to February4, 3, 2 and 1 percent discounts
April 1Unpaid taxes turn delinquent

Source: Florida Department of Revenue taxpayer page.

sections.h2: How does homestead work for a Miami Beach house?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption of up to $50,000 applies, and you file Form DR-501 with the property appraiser by March 1. The first $25,000 reaches school taxes too, while the second $25,000 touches only assessed value above $50,000 and skips school taxes.

  • You need to have made the home your permanent residence by January 1 of that tax year.
  • Renting the unit or moving out ends the exemption.
  • Under Save Our Homes, annual increases are limited to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The state chart lists a 2.7 percent cap for 2026.
  • A sale resets the property to just value on the next January 1.

That reset is why a buyer's first full bill in Miami Beach can look very different from yours.

sections.h2: Can I take my homestead savings to a new house if I move from Miami Beach?
sections.html:
Often yes, through portability. You must set up the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, not three years after the sale date. File Form DR-501T together with the DR-501 by March 1.

The state statute describes the transfer as the lesser of $500,000 or the gap between just value and assessed value on the old home. The statute page notes amendments that first apply to the 2027 roll, so confirm the current cap with the appraiser before you plan around a number.

Owners who cannot pay a full bill can ask the tax collector about a homestead deferral on Form DR-570, due March 31, or an installment plan requested by May 1.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax if I sell a Miami Beach house?
sections.html:
The tax lien sits ahead of the sale, so the balance gets paid out of the proceeds at closing. The title agent asks the tax collector for a payoff and proration for the year.

If the bill stays unpaid after April 1, the county can sell a tax certificate. The holder may apply for a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the issue year, per state statute. A homestead parcel opens at a bid that includes half of the latest assessed value.

Fix an unpaid bill before listing if you can. The tax collector in Miami-Dade runs 13 locations, online payment, and mobile offices, so there are several ways to clear a balance.

sections.h2: Where do I record a deed for a Miami Beach property?
sections.html:
Deeds for Miami Beach go to the Miami-Dade clerk at the county recorder's office, 20 NW 1st Avenue, Suite 5.246, Miami. Florida requires two witnesses on a deed, per section 689.01.

The clerk's page lists deed documentary stamps at 60 cents per $100, with a 45 cents per $100 surtax on transfers of real property other than a single-family residence. See the Miami-Dade records guide for the full fee list.

sections.h2: Who do I call with questions about a Miami Beach assessment?
sections.html:
Call the property appraiser at 305-375-4712 for the main downtown office at 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. A second branch operates in Cutler Bay at 10710 SW 211 Street.

Bring the folio number, your TRIM notice and any closing statement from a purchase. For bill balances, contact the tax collector instead.

faqs.q: Does Miami Beach send its own property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Miami-Dade County tax collector sends one combined bill that includes the city line of 5.8060 mills for operations plus 0.2693 for debt service.

faqs.q: When does a Miami Beach tax bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year after assessment. Before then, the November to February discounts of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent apply, and March is due at the full amount.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes cap if I sell?
faqs.a: The cap does not transfer with the sale, because a change of ownership resets value to just value. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, which needs Form DR-501T by March 1 and a new homestead within three years.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Miami Beach millage rate final?
faqs.a: Yes. The county chart lists adopted 2026 rates, with the city at 5.8060 mills. Individual parcels can fall on different lines, so check your own bill.

faqs.q: Who pays the doc stamps when I sell?
faqs.a: All parties to the deed are liable under state rules, regardless of which side agrees to pay. Your contract and title agent decide who actually pays.
